narrative:
The model estimated a 59.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, it judged that bad repayment was more likely than good repayment, placing your application above the bank’s risk limit, so the loan was denied. This is a risk estimate, not a finding of fact.

The strongest influence was your checking-account status: a negative balance below 0 DM pushed the decision toward bad credit. That situation is uncommon among approved applicants—only about 12.6% had it, compared with 59.2% who had no overdraft. The second most important factor was the amount requested. At 2,746 DM, it was slightly below the approved average of about 3,020 DM, so this factor actually worked in your favour, but not enough to offset the concerns. Third was your credit history. Having all credits paid at the bank is rare among approved applicants—only about 2.9%—and the model treated this unusual pattern as a warning sign, pushing toward bad credit.

To improve your position, speak to the lender about what specific evidence would correct or explain the checking-account and credit-history concerns. Reducing overdraft use, keeping accounts current, and, if possible, adding a reliable co-applicant or guarantor before reapplying would strengthen a future application.
